description: Update deploy/README.md and deploy/scan-input.md to describe the Design B model and to point at the setup script from FEAT-003. The headline change is removing the constraint that no longer exists: the docs currently state that the udev rule must be installed and the device node must exist BEFORE docker compose up, because Docker refuses to start a container whose declared device path is absent. After FEAT-002 there is no declared device path, so that whole ordering requirement is gone and must not be left in the docs to mislead a future reader. Several pre-existing doc defects are in scope because they sit in the same sections.
steps: In deploy/README.md, replace the manual Quick Start steps with a pointer to the script: clone or copy the deploy/ directory to the Pi, then `sudo ./setup.sh install`, then `sudo ./setup.sh status`. Keep a short prose statement of what install does so a reader is not required to read shell to understand the deployment. Keep the Supported Platform section and all the reference sections that follow.

Remove the ordering constraint wherever it appears. In deploy/README.md the Headless Scanner Input section contains an item reading approximately: 'The udev rule must be installed and /dev/pantry-scanner must exist before running docker compose up. Docker refuses to start a container whose declared device path does not exist.' Delete it and replace it with the new guarantee: the container starts regardless of whether the scanner is attached, and the scanner may be connected or disconnected at any time.

Add a short subsection explaining the new model, with the specifics a reader needs to trust it: the container bind-mounts the /dev/input directory rather than a single device node, so nodes udev creates later are visible without recreating the container; the application retries opening the device with backoff starting at 250ms and capped at 30s, so a newly attached scanner is picked up within 30 seconds; and the web UI is served the entire time, independent of scanner state.

Update every occurrence of /dev/pantry-scanner to /dev/input/pantry-scanner across both files, including the troubleshooting commands (`ls -l /dev/pantry-scanner`) and the docker inspect guidance. Note that the `docker inspect pantry | grep -A 5 Devices` suggestion is now obsolete because there is no Devices array — replace it with an instruction to check the Mounts array for the /dev/input bind mount and to consult `sudo ./setup.sh status` instead.

Fix the pre-existing wrong path in deploy/README.md: the udev install step reads `sudo cp pantry/udev/99-pantry-scanner.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/`, which is not a path that exists on the Pi. It should be /opt/pantry/udev/99-pantry-scanner.rules. Better still, state that `sudo ./setup.sh rule` generates and installs the rule from the detected device so hand-editing is unnecessary, and keep the manual path only as a fallback.

Fix the pre-existing broken numbering in the Headless Scanner Input Prerequisites section of deploy/README.md. It currently runs 1, 2, 3, 4 and then restarts at 2, 3, 4, 5, so there are two items numbered 2, 3, and 4. Renumber the section into a single coherent sequence.

Update the security rationale so it stays truthful. Both the README and the udev rules file explain that Pantry deliberately avoids adding its user to the `input` group to avoid read access to every keyboard on the machine. That reasoning still holds, but the mechanism changed: the container can now see every node in /dev/input, and what prevents it reading other devices is that those nodes are owned root:input mode 0600 while the udev rule grants only the scanner GROUP=65532 MODE=0640. Say this plainly rather than implying the container sees only one device.

Update the Automatic Updates considerations list. The existing bullet 'Container recreation will drop any attached barcode scanner session' is now materially wrong in its implication — the session is dropped but the listener reconnects on its own within 30 seconds. Reword accordingly. Add a note that `sudo ./setup.sh freeze` masks the update timer while iterating on deployment changes, because a five-minute timer that pulls latest and recreates the container makes debugging irreproducible, and `thaw` restores it.

Add a short note that the container image is distroless, so `docker exec pantry sh` does not work and runtime introspection is limited to `docker compose logs pantry`, `GET /health`, and `sudo ./setup.sh status`. This saves the next reader from a dead end.

In the Troubleshooting section, restructure the scanner guidance around the distinction that actually matters now: scanner absent is a supported state (container running, /health ok, scanner.connected false, UI fully usable) versus scanner present but unreadable (node exists but health reports connected:false). For the latter, give the three causes in the order worth checking — the udev rule did not match the device so no symlink was created, the node's group is not 65532, or the container is missing the supplementary group. Point at `sudo ./setup.sh status` as the first step in all cases.

In deploy/scan-input.md, apply the same changes: new device path, no pre-start ordering requirement, no systemd units, GROUP=65532 consistently (the file currently shows GROUP="pantry" in two rule examples, which contradicts the numeric GID used everywhere else), and the reconnect guarantee. Do not add TAG+="systemd" or SYSTEMD_WANTS anywhere.

Confirm no documentation anywhere instructs the reader to install a pantry.service unit, to run `udevadm trigger --action=add` without a subsystem filter, or to run `docker compose up -d` by hand as the normal path. The normal path is the setup script.
Commit with a message like `docs: describe scanner hot-plug deployment model`.
acceptance_criteria: Neither deploy/README.md nor deploy/scan-input.md states or implies that the device must exist before the container is started.
Both files use /dev/input/pantry-scanner exclusively; no reference to /dev/pantry-scanner remains.
deploy/README.md Quick Start directs the reader to `sudo ./setup.sh install` followed by `sudo ./setup.sh status`.
A subsection documents the hot-plug model including the 30-second worst-case pickup and the fact that the UI is served independently of scanner state.
The udev install path is corrected to /opt/pantry/udev/... and `setup.sh rule` is presented as the primary method.
The Headless Scanner Input Prerequisites section has a single coherent numbering sequence with no duplicated numbers.
The security rationale states that per-device scoping comes from node ownership and mode, not from the container seeing only one node.
The obsolete `docker inspect ... Devices` guidance is replaced, and the distroless limitation is documented.
Troubleshooting distinguishes 'scanner absent (supported)' from 'scanner present but unreadable' and lists the three causes for the latter.
deploy/scan-input.md uses GROUP="65532" in all rule examples.
No documentation references a pantry.service unit, an unfiltered udevadm trigger, or TAG+="systemd".
verification: `grep -rni 'before running docker compose up\|refuses to start' deploy/*.md` produces no output.
`grep -n 'setup.sh install\|setup.sh status\|setup.sh rule\|setup.sh freeze' deploy/README.md` shows the script is referenced for install, status, rule, and freeze.
Read the renumbered Prerequisites section and confirm by eye that each ordinal appears exactly once.
`git diff master --stat -- deploy/` shows changes confined to README.md, scan-input.md, and the files already changed by FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
